== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' lived in Linlithgow, Linlithgowshire. His wife was '''Agnes Eastone''', whose surname also appears in the parish records as '''Daston'''. Their children included

* [[Glasgow-4098|Hellen Glasgow]], baptised 22 December 1668
* John Glasgow
* Thomas Glasgow

as named in the Linlithgow registers.<ref>Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', Linlithgow Old Parish Registers; the individual entries are cited on each child's profile.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Father confidence review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-1103]] is assessed at 76% (probable). The 1644 Linlithgow transcript names father Thomas Glasgow and mother Hellin Bryse. The selected Thomas-1103 was baptised in1612, giving a compatible32-year generation; his maintained account already includes this adult household. Name, timing and central-Scotland setting favour the selection, while no source connects the1612 child to the1644 father.

This76% assesses the complete profile-to-profile placement, including the unproved Thomas child/adult identification. The named Thomas father in the1644 record itself is explicit. The Inveresk Thomas may be distinct; no original image newly inspected.

Next useful test: Compare adult Thomas occupations, residences and witnesses across the Linlithgow and Inveresk households.

Source basis already held: [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F0497604&tab=this Findmypast, Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564-1929: John Glasgow, 1644, record SCOT/OPR/BAP/0497604]. No new original was inspected in this review. This is an assessment of an existing attachment, not a new father.


=== Selected uncertain family — 16 October 2026 ===

Select John [[Glasgow-1105]] and Agnes Eastone-3 as the uncertain working parents of Thomas [[Glasgow-1226]], the father with Catherine Clarkson/Classon at Uphall from 1717 and Livingston by 1730. This selects possible identity with their named Linlithgow child Thomas [[Glasgow-1242]] of 1675, while retaining both profile accounts. That child would be about 42 at the 1717 Margaret entry and about 60 at the 1735 Hellen entry: later fatherhood, but chronologically possible. The existing Glasgow-1242 account also represents a Thomas/Jean Duncan household at Uphall in 1704. Recurring Thomas name, the same Uphall parish and a plausible succession of households provide a more specific route than the removed Kilbirnie-minister parents. The 1675 parent clause belongs directly to the child account; transferring it to the Clarkson adult depends wholly on the uncertain identity.

The 1675 child, the Duncan adult and the Clarkson adult may represent one, two or three men. There is no inspected age, occupation, marriage, widowhood or probate bridge. The 1701 Duncan marriage is reported family information, not a newly inspected register. No death of Jean, remarriage to Catherine or overlap resolution is invented. The differing Philip 1711 dates in the Thomas research compilation and the Glasgow-1242 biography, and the omission of a mother in the latter’s indexed child, do not establish a continuous Duncan household or certain maternity. They are not two independent confirmations. Catherine’s indexed surname variants remain as recorded. The before 1700 boundary for the Clarkson adult and the 2/21 February 1675 date discrepancy in the child account remain unchanged. The 1666 St Cuthbert’s Thomas-1311, child of Alexander and Issobell Anderson, remains a compatible identity alternative, albeit with fatherhood at about 51–69 in 1717–1735. His possible identification with the Edinburgh writer whose testament was indexed in 1691 is unproved and cannot be used to exclude him. The retained 1766 grave link is an unverified namesake comparison, not an established death for the Clarkson adult. The 1663 Thomas-3091 and an otherwise unrecorded local Thomas also remain possible. No identity merge or live attachment is performed. John was the son of [[Glasgow-1106|Thomas Glasgow]] and Hellin Bryse. The Eastone/Daston spelling varies between the register indexes; no other record has been found to give John's own birth or death.
